comments.body:
ROOT-CAUSE EVIDENCE, captured BEFORE any kickstart (this ticket's first AC requires that ordering —
forcing a sync first would have destroyed it).

`launchctl print gui/$(id -u)/com.navapbc.rebar-dev-update`:
    state          = not running
    run interval   = 3600 seconds
    properties     = runatload | inferred program
    LAST EXIT CODE = 1
    stdout path    = /Users/joeoakhart/.local/state/rebar-dev/launchd.out.log
    stderr path    = /Users/joeoakhart/.local/state/rebar-dev/launchd.err.log

SO THE AGENT IS NOT IDLE — IT IS FIRING HOURLY AND FAILING EVERY TIME. That distinction matters: a
stopped agent looks like a stopped agent, whereas this one is alive, scheduled, and silently
unsuccessful, which is why nobody noticed for days.

THREE CORROBORATING TIMESTAMPS in /Users/joeoakhart/.local/state/rebar-dev/:
    launchd.err.log   0 bytes, created Jul 10 12:03
    launchd.out.log   0 bytes, created Jul 10 12:03
    last-good.sha     41 bytes, Jul 17 08:16
    directory mtime   Jul 31 21:47  (i.e. TODAY, minutes before this capture)

Read together: the directory is touched on every run, so the agent DID run today; it exits 1; and it
has written NOTHING to either log since the files were created on Jul 10. **An updater that fails
hourly with exit 1 and produces zero diagnostic output is the real defect** — the stale build is only
its symptom. Whatever fails, fails before any redirection takes effect, or its output is discarded.

The last recorded GOOD sha is Jul 17, while the installed
site-packages/rebar/llm/criteria/overlay.py is dated Jul 27 17:10. So the rollback guard is pinning a
Jul-27 build while the last verified-good checkpoint is ten days older still — the two records
disagree, and neither matches origin/main.

DO NOT kickstart before capturing whatever the underlying script writes when run by hand: the
0-byte logs mean the launchd redirection is not carrying its output, so run the updater's script
directly in a shell to see the actual error. Kickstarting first re-runs it under the same broken
redirection and yields the same silence.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
REPAIRED. The updater ran green for the first time in two weeks: exit 0, and last-good.sha advanced
4dd9172b9 (Jul 17) -> 25fa6107f (main tip). TWO root causes, both needed — neither alone explains
every symptom, and fixing only the first still failed.

FIRST, A CORRECTION TO MY OWN EARLIER REPORT ON THIS TICKET. I said the build was ~4 days stale and
that the 0-byte launchd logs were the defect. Both wrong:
 * The failure began 2026-07-17T16:23:19Z, immediately after the last success at 15:16:40Z —
   294 CONSECUTIVE FAILED RUNS over TWO WEEKS, not 4 days. The Jul-27 code mtime I measured was a
   MANUAL pin (the doc documents that operation), which is what made the two records disagree.
 * The 0-byte launchd.{out,err}.log are BY DESIGN — the script redirects its own output to
   update.log (183 KB, and the actual evidence). I had not read update.log. Reading it named the
   cause on the first line.

ROOT CAUSE A — a stale uv SHADOWS a good one on the updater's own PATH.
  ~/.local/bin/uv          0.7.18  (2025-07-01), an orphaned 35 MB standalone binary
  /opt/homebrew/bin/uv     0.12.0  (2026-07-28), satisfies pipx
  ~/.langflow/uv                   the copy the standalone installer actually manages
Line 33 exported PATH="${HOME}/.local/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin:..." — ~/.local/bin FIRST — so pipx
resolved 0.7.18, and pipx >=1.8 requires uv>=0.9.17. Every run died at that check.
Reproduced directly: under that exact PATH, `command -v uv` -> ~/.local/bin/uv, 0.7.18.
`uv self update` CANNOT fix it: it refuses because the standalone installer manages ~/.langflow/uv,
not this path. FIX: put /opt/homebrew/bin ahead of ~/.local/bin. ~/.local/bin stays on PATH — it
holds the pipx-installed `rebar` shim the smoke test invokes; only precedence changed.

ROOT CAUSE B — the pipx venv was PINNED to the pip backend, and pip cannot resolve this package.
Fixing A alone STILL FAILED. ~/.local/pipx/venvs/nava-rebar/pipx_metadata.json recorded
`backend = pip`, and pipx's own help states the rule: the backend "Defaults to ... 'uv' when uv is
available ... else 'pip'. EXISTING VENVS ALWAYS HONOR THEIR" original backend. So a good uv on PATH
changed nothing. pip then failed with `error: resolution-too-deep` — this package installs NINE
extras (agents,dev,eval,grounding,grounding-t2,mcp,reviewbot,tracing,ui) and pip backtracks through
click/fsspec and gives up. pipx's surface message ("pip seemed to fail to build package: click...")
is MISLEADING — nothing was building; the resolver quit.
Proved not overridable: `pipx install ... --force --backend uv` was IGNORED — same
resolution-too-deep, metadata still `backend = pip`. FIX: `pipx uninstall nava-rebar` then a fresh
install, which adopted `backend = uv` and succeeded.

A WRONG FIX I TRIED AND REVERTED, recorded so nobody repeats it: `--backend pip`, which is the
workaround ticket 72ca documents for this error. It DOES clear cause A's error, and then fails on
cause B. **--backend pip is not viable for this package** — uv is a hard requirement here, not a
preference, because only uv resolves the nine-extra graph. 72ca's documented workaround should say
so.

MUTATION CHECK: restoring the old PATH order reproduces the exact uv error, so the one-line fix is
load-bearing rather than decorative. Post-fix state verified clean: backend=uv, nava-rebar 0.10.1,
`rebar list --help` exit 0, script diff = the PATH line plus its explanation, install line untouched.

STEP-6 REPLICATION of the reported symptom: the GLOBAL build now parses the dict-shaped `activate`
— `registry.effective_criteria('.')` returns 44 effective criteria where it previously raised
CriteriaError. The silent gate degradation is gone.

AWS IS NOT INVOLVED. The operator suggested AWS CLI access might be relevant; it is not. The updater
installs from `git+https://github.com/navapbc/rebar.git` and touches no AWS service. No AWS calls
were made.

THIS TICKET STAYS OPEN. The ENVIRONMENT is repaired, but two ACs are code work and are NOT done:
distinguishing an overlay CriteriaError from an LLM outage, and naming the installed build as the
suspect in that case. Those are the durable fix — the reason this cost two weeks is that a broken
INSTALL presented as an unreviewable TICKET. The environment repair does not prevent a recurrence.

compiled_state.description:
# The global rebar build is 4 days stale, and it SILENTLY disables the LLM tier of plan review

## Context / Problem
This machine's global `rebar`/`rebar-mcp` is supposed to track `origin/main` HOURLY via a
rollback-guarded LaunchAgent (documented in `docs/local-env-main-tracking.local.md`). IT HAS NOT RUN
SINCE 2026-07-27 17:10 — measured from the mtime of
`/Users/joeoakhart/.local/pipx/venvs/nava-rebar/lib/python3.14/site-packages/rebar/llm/criteria/overlay.py`,
and corroborated by the venv directory's own mtime. Today is 2026-07-31, so the global build is ~4
days behind main.

**THE FAILURE MODE IS SILENT DEGRADATION OF THE REVIEW GATE, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS A BUG AND NOT
HOUSEKEEPING.** `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` carries `activate` as a DICT (scoped per review type),
which main's overlay parser accepts — `git show origin/main:src/rebar/llm/criteria/overlay.py | grep
"must be a list of ids"` returns NOTHING. The stale global build predates that: its overlay.py DOES
contain that check and raises `CriteriaError: 'activate' must be a list of ids, got dict`. Support
landed in `f3dbe32b0b` (2026-07-27, "3ba4: Scope project criteria by review type") and
`7f4c650114` (2026-07-28).

MEASURED consequence of running `rebar review-plan <id> --ref HEAD` with the global build in this repo:

    "llm_ran": false,
    "llm_unavailable": true,
    "llm_error": "step 'review@then/assemble' failed: criteria overlay .../.rebar/criteria_routing.json:
                  'activate' must be a list of ids, got dict"
    "verdict": "INDETERMINATE"

The command EXITS 2 and emits a sidecar. It does not present as a broken install; it presents as a
plan that could not be reviewed. The DET tier still runs and reports pass/fail per criterion, so the
output looks substantive. An operator or agent reading that verdict would reasonably conclude the
TICKET is the problem. **No LLM review happened at all.**

The worktree build parses the same file fine — `registry.effective_criteria('.')` returns 44 effective
criteria — so this is purely the stale global install, not a repo defect.

## Why this matters beyond one command
AGENTS.md already warns to run the repo checkout's build rather than a stale global install, and gives
the reason as "silently ignores newer config keys". This incident shows the consequence is worse than
ignoring a key: an unrelated-looking INDETERMINATE on the claim gate. Any agent that trusts
`which rebar` gets it. The MCP server is affected the same way and, per the local docs, will not
hot-reload.

## Approach
Two separable pieces:
 1. DIAGNOSE why the LaunchAgent stopped. Check `launchctl print gui/$(id -u)/com.navapbc.rebar-dev-update`
    for its last exit status, and the agent's own log, before forcing a sync. A rollback-guarded updater
    that silently gave up 4 days ago has its own failure to explain — forcing a sync hides the evidence.
    Force it only after capturing that state:
    `launchctl kickstart -k gui/$(id -u)/com.navapbc.rebar-dev-update`.
 2. MAKE THE STALENESS LOUD rather than silent. A gate run whose LLM tier dies on a CONFIG-PARSE error
    from the installed build is not the same as an LLM outage, and collapsing both into
    `llm_unavailable` + INDETERMINATE is what made this cost time. A `CriteriaError` while loading the
    overlay is a CONFIGURATION fault: it should surface distinctly (its own verdict reason or a loud
    warning naming the installed build's version), so the reader is pointed at the install rather than
    at the plan.

## Scope
- The LaunchAgent / updater: diagnosis first, then a sync.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/` — distinguish a config-parse failure from an LLM outage in the verdict's
  `llm_error` / reason surfacing.
- Possibly a startup or gate-time warning when the running build's commit is far behind the repo's.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] the reason the hourly updater stopped after 2026-07-27 17:10 is recorded on this ticket, captured
      BEFORE any forced re-sync
- [ ] the global build parses `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` with a dict-shaped `activate`, evidenced by
      a `rebar review-plan` run whose output shows `llm_ran: true`
- [ ] a test asserts an overlay `CriteriaError` raised while assembling criteria is reported distinctly
      from an LLM outage, so it cannot present as a plain INDETERMINATE
- [ ] [operator-attested] the verdict text or warning for that case names the INSTALLED BUILD as the
      suspect, evidenced by the observed output pasted on this ticket

file_impact.reason: distinguish an overlay CriteriaError from an LLM outage
assert a config-parse fault is not reported as an LLM outage
